articles.title: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior sent off for hair-pulling in victory over Villarreal
articles.summary: Yan Diomandé earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinícius Júnior was sent off for hair pulling.
body: Vinícius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he had pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.

José Mourinho’s side battled through the final stages with 10 men, holding on to win and provisionally going third. But the red card left a bitter taste for Real, with Vinícius running the risk of a potential ban which could keep him out of El Clásico on 25 October.
“I don’t know what’s going on with the referees, with this red card, I don’t understand,” said the Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni. “But the most important thing is the victory.”

Kylian Mbappé was fit to start the match for Madrid after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break. There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from others.

articles.title: USWNT exposed by ruthless Spain as early goals settle heavyweight friendly
articles.summary: Guijarro and Navarro score in opening 14 minutes. US midfield and defensive lapses exposed by Spain. Yohannes misses penalty as US fightback falls short. In less than a year’s time, the United States and Spain will almost certainly arrive in Brazil as the top two contenders to win the Women’s World…
body: This month’s pair of friendlies between the two sides are taking place with caveats. Both sides are missing several of their most important players to injuries. The opening match in Brazil is 258 days away. Spain have booked their place, but the US still have to actually qualify for the World Cup, through a regional tournament that begins next month.

Even without full-strength rosters, a meeting between these two teams is a compelling bill. And in their first of two friendlies, on Saturday in Washington DC, Spain had the upper hand, scoring twice in the first 14 minutes of a 2-0 win.
“You can’t afford to go 2-0 down against the best team in the world, especially the way we conceded those goals,” US coach Emma Hayes said. “That’s the learning.”

In just the fifth meeting between the two sides and the first since 11 October 2022 – before Spain broke through to win the 2023 World Cup – the reigning champions took advantage of defensive lapses and the US midfield’s struggles. After trailing by two goals for the first time under Emma Hayes, the Americans played a much-improved second half, but failures to convert chances and a stopped penalty kept them scoreless.

articles.title: Carrick ‘massively disappointed’ after United drop points against 10-man Spurs
articles.summary: Six points from six games is worst start since 1986. De Zerbi praises Spurs’ character after late equaliser. Michael Carrick was left “massively disappointed” by Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham at Old Trafford and admitted they need more points after managing six from their opening six…
body: This is United’s poorest start to the season since 1986, Saturday’s draw coming when conceding Dominic Solanke’s added-time equaliser for 10-man Spurs, following Rodrigo Bentancur’s 78th-minute red card. The midfielder was sent off five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo’s opener had left United heading for only a second league victory.

Carrick said: “I am massively disappointed with the result, for sure. A mixed performance. I’m not happy with the amount of points that we’ve had so far. There’s no hiding from that. I think it could have been different for a couple of little things here or there, but the reality is the reality, we’ve got to accept it, you know. We need to put things in a direction, in a positive direction quite quickly, that’s pretty plain.”

articles.title: Ulster playing games like they're training sessions - Murphy
articles.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
body: Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.
Having opened the campaign with a home defeat by Edinburgh and a 33-33 draw in Glasgow, Murphy's side remain winless on the domestic front before starting their European campaign next week.
"We're still very much in the early part of the season. We've got three our four players coming back in for their first games this weekend," said Murphy.
"The flow of the team hasn't completely settled in. At the moment, we're playing matches like they're training sessions.

body: For the second time in successive home Premier League games, Manchester United failed to beat opponents reduced to 10 men.
For the third time in as many seasons, a United manager finds himself under severe pressure before the clocks have gone back.

Four weeks ago, Manchester City needed an incorrect video assistant referee (VAR) decision to take advantage of an ineffective United performance after Phil Foden had been shown a red card in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

On Saturday, the damage was self-inflicted as a Spurs side, who had given every indication of being unable to score before Rodrigo Bentancur's headfirst charge at Luke Shaw just five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo's opener, came up with an injury-time equaliser.

articles.title: 'Reminds me of Muller' - Naderi proving worth in Rangers revival
articles.summary: After a slow start to his Rangers career, striker Ryan Naderi is playing an integral role in the club's title challenge and proving his doubters wrong.
body: A previously unfancied striker is playing a crucial role in Rangers' revival - and even earning comparisons with Germany legend Thomas Muller.

Ryan Naderi pounced for a first-half double against Kilmarnock as Derek McInnes' side overcame the disruption of the extended international break to earn a sixth straight league win and rise to the top of the Scottish Premiership.
That outcome enhanced a turnaround in fortunes for Rangers after the disappointment of their European exit, having also taken just a point from their first two Premiership games.
They now lie a point ahead of Celtic, who visit Motherwell on Sunday under pressure to regain their place at the top.

articles.title: How Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski feels about starting NLCS Game 1 vs. Tarik Skubal
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Milwaukee Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski is officially set to start Game 1 of the National League Championship Series. His opponent on the mound for the Los Angeles Dodgers? Tarik Skubal.
body: “I’m not really looking at them (the opposing star pitcher), I’m looking at the lineup more than him,” Misiorowski told reporters Saturday, via Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. “For me personally, it doesn’t really mean that much to face a guy like that. Like, obviously it’s cool… But I’m just hoping that these guys (Brewers’ lineup) can do their job and handle business with him, and let me do my thing.”

It projects to be a highly competitive NLCS. The Dodgers’ pitching is deep, but the Brewers’ pitching is rather underrated. Of course, everyone knows the name Jacob Misiorowski. The fact that Milwaukee’s bullpen is strong is also a well known fact. However, starters such as Logan Henderson and Robert Gasser should not be overlooked.

The attention of the MLB world on Saturday night will be on the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians as they play Game 5 of their ALDS clash. The winner of that series will play the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALCS.

As for the NLCS, Milwaukee is set to host Los Angeles in Game 1 on Sunday night, with first pitch scheduled for 8 PM ET. Misiorowski will do everything he can to place his team in a quality position to win Game 1.

body: Quarterback Cale Hellum ran the length of two football fields by himself in Saturday’s win over Tulane. He finished the game with 223 rushing yards on 38 carries and two touchdowns. Tulane finally gained a 10-7 lead in the third quarter after an 11-play 68yard touchdown drive, which was their first of the game.
Army kept up the whole way through the game. Neither team held a lead by more than a possession.

articles.title: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's underperformance with his players
articles.summary: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.
body: Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.
Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that turned a broken season into a third-place finish?
points: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game.
With the ball, without the ball, we were off it.
A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.

articles.title: WWE Money In The Bank 2026 Results As Roman Reigns Beats LA Knight In Another Clean Win
articles.summary: Roman Reigns beat LA Knight, once again retaining the WWE World Heavyweight Championship with a solo win and no interference. Roman Reigns and LA Knight have been feuding, on and off, since Roman’s record-breaking 1,316-day reign.
body: Top heel stable 946 has been lurking in the shadows, and Royce Keys' group has become stronger with each passing week. With WarGames around the corner, Reigns crossing paths with the (kayfabe) gang-affiliated stable is inevitable. 946 made an appearance after the match and brawled with the Usos and Solo Sikoa.

The match began with a deliberate, slow pace from both combatants, who talked trash as they sized each other up. Fans were more into LA Knight than Roman, and Knight got out to an early lead, hitting a shoulder tackle that knocked Reigns to his feet. Knight kept the pressure on Reigns with 10-count punches, but Reigns came back with a pair of clotheslines.

Reigns hit a third flying clothesline to a mixed reaction. Reigns hit a boot flooring Knight, but missed a Superman Punch. Knight came back with a clothesline of his own. Roman tried a back body drop, but Knight countered with a kick and dumped Reigns to the outside.

articles.title: NFL Gameday Guide: Jags and Eagles land in London
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars return to London this week to play what will mark their 15th and 16th regular-season games in England's capital since 2013, featuring as part of the league's 44th and 45th games in the UK since 2007 as well as a record slate of nine international matchups in 2026.
body: It will see Jags punter Logan Cooke play in an NFL-record 10th international game to surpass former Jacksonville offensive lineman Tyler Shatley, per ESPN stats.

But this has a different feel to that of the Jags teams from years gone by, who have monopolised London without ever truly inserting themselves among football's Super Bowl contenders. The 2017 team that stunned the NFL to reach the AFC Championship Game, perhaps, being the exception to that rule.

This time they arrive to take on the Philadelphia Eagles behind a true MVP candidate in Trevor Lawrence and a head coach in Liam Coen knocking on the door of the elite. It is not a team brimming with star names, but instead an expertly-drilled reflection of their coach's vision for contention.
The Jags are 3-1 and purring at the top of the AFC South, their one blemish a defeat to the Denver Broncos in which they can been control before letting the game slip away.
